questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x \sqrt{1+y}+y \sqrt{1+x}=0$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Given, } x \sqrt{1+y}+y \sqrt{1+x}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x \sqrt{1+y}=-y \sqrt{1+x} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(x \sqrt{1+y})^2=(-y \sqrt{1+x})^2
\end{aligned}$\begin{array}{lr}
\Rightarrow & x^2(1+y)=y^2(1+x) \\
\Rightarrow & x^2-y^2=y^2 x-x^2 y \\
\Rightarrow & (x-y)(x+y)=x y(y-x) \\
\Rightarrow & x+y=-x y \\
\Rightarrow & x+y+x y=0 \\
\Rightarrow & y=$\frac{-x}{1+x}=$-1+$\frac{1}{1+x}$
\end{array}$
Differentiating w.r.t, $ x $\frac{d y}{d x}=$-$\frac{1}{(1+x)^2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y=\tan ^{-1} \left(\frac{\sqrt{x}-x}{1+x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right), then $ y^{\prime}(1)$ is equal to$
questions.solution:
Given, $\begin{aligned} y & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x}-x}{1+x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right) \\ y & =\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x}-x}{1+\sqrt{x} \cdot x}\right) \\ y & =\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{x})-\tan ^{-1} x \\ & {\left[\because \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x-y}{1+x y}\right)=\tan ^{-1} x-\tan ^{-1} y\right] }\end{aligned}$
Differentiating w.r.t $xy^{\prime}(x)=\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{1+x} \times \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}-\frac{1}{1+x^2}$
Now, $\quad y^{\prime}(1)=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{4}$

questions.q: At $x=\frac{\pi^2}{4}, \frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1}(\cos \sqrt{x})+\sec ^{-1}\left(e^x\right)\right)=$
questions.solution:
$\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1}(\cos \sqrt{x})+\sec ^{-1}\left(\mathrm{e}^x\right)\right)=\frac{(-\sin \sqrt{x})}{1+\cos ^2 \sqrt{x}} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}\right)+\frac{1}{e^x \sqrt{e^{2 x}-1}} \cdot e^x$
but when $x=\frac{\pi^2}{4}=-\frac{-\sin \frac{\pi}{2}}{1+\cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{e^{\pi^2 / 2}-1}}=-\frac{1}{\pi}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{e^{\pi^2 / 2}-1}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The slope of the tangent to the curve $x=3 t^2+1$, $y=t^3-1$ at $x=1$ is:
questions.solution:
Given curve is $x=3 t^2+1$


Second curve is $y=t^3-1$

$\therefore \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y}{d t} \times \frac{d t}{d x}=3 t^2 \times \frac{1}{6 t}=\frac{t}{2}$
But from (i) when $x=1$
we have $1=3 t^2+1 \Rightarrow 3 t^2=0 \Rightarrow t=0$
$\therefore$ When $\mathrm{x}=1$ then $\mathrm{t}=0 \quad \therefore \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathbf{0}$
Hence, slope of the tangent to the curve $=0$

questions.q: If $y^x=e^{y-x}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
questions.solution: Here, $\mathrm{y}^{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x}}$Taking log on both sides, we get$\begin{aligned} \\ & \log y^x=\log e^{y-x} \\ \\ & \quad\left(\because \log a^b=b \log a \text{$ and $} \log e=1\right) \\ \end{aligned} \Rightarrow x \log y=(y-x) \log e \Rightarrow x \log y=y-x \ldots(i)$On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get$\frac{d}{d x}(x \log y)=\frac{d}{d x}(y-x)$(using product rule)$\begin{aligned} \\ & \Rightarrow x\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+\log y(1)=\frac{d y}{d x}-1 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}\left(\frac{x}{y}-1\right)=-1-\log y \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{y}{(1+\log y) y}-1\right]=-(1+\log y) \\ \\ & \qquad \quad\left[\because \text{$ from $eq. }(i) \cdot x=\frac{y}{(1+\log y)}\right] \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{1-1-\log y}{1+\log y}\right]=-(1+\log y) \\ \end{aligned} \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{(1+\log y)^2}{-\log y} \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(1+\log y)^2}{\log y}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\sqrt{1+\cos ^2\left(\mathrm{x}^2\right)}$, then the value of $f^{\prime}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
On differentiating (i) w.r.t.x, we get
$f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{-2 \sin x^2 \cos x^2}{\sqrt{1+\cos ^2 x^2}}(x)$

Put, $x=\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}$ in (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{f}^{\prime}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\right)=-\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \cdot \frac{\sin 2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}{\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{2}}} \\
& =-\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \cdot \frac{\sin \frac{\pi}{2}}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}}=-\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{6}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The derivative of $e^{x^3}$ with respect to $\log x$ is
questions.solution:
Let $y=\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}^3}, \mathrm{z}=\log \mathrm{x}$
On differentiating w.r.t.x, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=e^{x^3}\left(3 x^2\right)=3 x^2 e^{x^3} \text{ and } \frac{d z}{d x}=\frac{1}{x}$
$\therefore \frac{d y}{d z}=\frac{\frac{d y}{d x}}{\frac{d z}{d x}}=\frac{3 x^2 e^{x^3}}{\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}=3 x^3 e^{x^3}$

questions.q: If $y=\sqrt{\left(\frac{1+\cos 2 \theta}{1-\cos 2 \theta}\right)}$, then $\frac{d y}{d \theta}$ at $\theta=\frac{3 \pi}{4}$ is :
questions.solution:
$y=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos 2 \theta}{1-\cos 2 \theta}}$
$\Rightarrow y=\sqrt{\frac{2 \cos ^2 \theta}{2 \sin ^2 \theta}}=\sqrt{\cot ^2 \theta}$
$\Rightarrow y=\cot \theta$
Differentiate w.r.t. ' $\theta$ ', we get: $\frac{d y}{d \theta}=-\operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta$
Now, $\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}\right)_{\theta=\frac{3 \pi}{4}}=-\operatorname{cosec}^2 \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)
$=-\operatorname{cosec}^2$\left(\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\operatorname{cosec}^2 \frac{\pi}{4}=-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ If } 2^{x}+2^{y}=2^{x+y} \text{, then } \frac{d y}{d x}=$
questions.solution: $On differentiating \begin{array}{l} 2^{x} \log 2+2^{y} \log 2 \cdot \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}} \\ =2^{x} \cdot 2^{y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}} \cdot \log 2+2^{y} \cdot 2^{x} \log 2 \\ \Rightarrow 2^{x}+2^{y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=2^{x+y} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+2^{x+y} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{2^{x+y}-2^{x}}{2^{y}-2^{x+y}} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{2^{x}+2^{y}-2^{x}}{2^{y}-2^{x}-2^{y}}=-2^{y-x} \end{array}$

questions.q: If $x=\frac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$ and $y=\frac{2 t}{1+t^{2}}$, then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to :
questions.solution: Let $x=\frac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$ and $y=\frac{2 t}{1+t^{2}}$ Put $t=\tan \theta$, we get $x=\frac{1-\tan ^{2} \theta}{1+\tan ^{2} \theta}$ and $y=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^{2} \theta}\Rightarrow x=\cos 2 \theta$ and $y=\sin 2 \theta\therefore \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=-2 \sin 2 \theta$ and $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} \theta}=2 \cos 2 \theta$ Now, $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} \theta} \times \frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dx}}=-\frac{\cos 2 \theta}{\sin 2 \theta}=-\frac{x}{y}$

questions.solution: We have $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{1+\cos \frac{x}{2}}{1-\cos \frac{x}{2}}}\right)=\frac{d}{d x}\left[\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{1+\left(2 \cos ^{2} \frac{x}{4}-1\right)}{1-\left(1-2 \sin ^{2} \frac{x}{4}\right)}}\right]=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\left.\frac{2 \cos ^{2} \frac{x}{4}}{2 \sin ^{2} \frac{x}{4}}\right)}\right.=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\cot ^{2} \frac{x}{4}}\right)=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \cot \frac{x}{4}\right)=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\tan ^{-1} \tan \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{x}{4}\right)\right)=\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{x}{4}\right)=0-\frac{1}{4}=-\frac{1}{4}$

questions.q: Let $f(x+y)=f(x) \cdot f(y)$ for all $x, y$ where $f(0) \neq 0$ If $f(5)=2$ and $f^{\prime}(0)=3,$ then $f^{\prime}(5)$ is equal to-
questions.solution: $f^{\prime}(5)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(5+h)-f(5)}{h}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(5+h)-f(5+0)}{h}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(5) \cdot f(h)-f(5)+f(0)}{h}(\because f(x+y)=f(x), f(y)$ for all $x, y)=\left(\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(h)-f(0)}{h}\right) \cdot f(5)=f^{\prime}(0) \cdot f(5)=3 \times 2=6$

questions.q: For the function $f(x)=\frac{x^{100}}{100}+\frac{x^{99}}{99}+\ldots \frac{x^{2}}{2}+x+1\mathrmf^{\prime}(1)=\mathrm{mf}^{\prime}(0),$ where $\mathrm{m}$ is equal to
questions.solution: Given, $f(x)=\frac{x^{100}}{100}+\frac{x^{99}}{99}+\ldots+\frac{x^{2}}{2}+x+1\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{100 x^{99}}{100}+\frac{99 x^{98}}{99}+\ldots+\frac{2 x}{2}+1+0\left[\because \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{\mathrm{n}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{nx}^{\mathrm{n}-1}\right]\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}^{99}+\mathrm{x}^{98}+\ldots+\mathrm{x}+1$...(i) Putting $\mathrm{x}=1$, we get $f^{\prime}(1)=\underbrace{(1)^{99}+1^{98}+\ldots+1+1}_{100 \text{ times }}=\underbrace{1+1+1 \ldots+1+1}_{100 \text{ times }}\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=100$...(ii) Again, putting $\mathrm{x}=0$, we get $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0)=0+0+\ldots+0+1 \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0)=1$...(iii) From eqs. (ii) and(iii), we get; $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=100 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(0)$ Hence, $m=100$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If \(y=x^{x^2}\), then \($\frac{d y}{d x}$\) is equal to
questions.solution:
Consider \(y=x^{x^2} \Rightarrow \ln y=x² \ln x\)
\begin{aligned} $\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=$2 x \ln x+x² \cdot $\frac{1}{x}=$x(1+2 \ln x) \\ $\frac{d y}{d x}=$x^{x^2} \cdot x(1+2 \ln x)=x^{x^2+1}(1+2 \ln x)
\end{aligned}\)
